items.q: And Robenoff was one of them. He was getting his group together. And he would talk to me, and he had, oh, two, three other guys, would say, 'What do you think? Who's the best? Who's in this chair who's good?'

ctx.x: Seventh Avenue, between Seventh and Sixth, and they were regular rehearsal halls just for these particular bandleaders that had these particular things in mind. And I know in one instance when they were hiring musicians, they used to have like the first alto player, three deep, you know, would have two other guys sitting on the side, and they'd take one arrangement, and they'd have this guy come and sit in. They would play the arrangement down, and he'd sit five minutes, and -- "Well, let's try this guy," you…

Oh, there were quite a few bandleaders that I was connected with that had the same idea. And Robenoff was one of them. He was getting his group together. And he would talk to me, and he had, oh, two, three other guys, would say, "What do you think? Who's the best? Who's in this chair who's good?" And, of course, it put us on the spot because all eyes were there, you know.
